{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
{-# LANGUAGE DataKinds #-}
{-# LANGUAGE GADTs #-}

module GrpcShutdown where

import Data.Word (Word32, Word64)
import Data.Int (Int32)
import Data.IORef
import Control.Concurrent
import Control.Concurrent.STM
import Control.Monad (when, unless, forever, void)
import qualified Data.Map.Strict as Map
import System.Clock

-- | Connection tracking for graceful shutdown
data ConnectionState = ConnectionState
  { csActiveRequests  :: !Word32
  , csMaxRequests     :: !Word32
  , csDrainDeadline   :: !Word64
  , csCreatedAt       :: !Word64
  , csGracePeriodMs   :: !Word32
  } deriving (Show)

data ShutdownPhase = Running | Draining | Terminated
  deriving (Show, Eq)

data ServerState = ServerState
  { ssConnections   :: TVar (Map.Map Int ConnectionState)
  , ssPhase         :: TVar ShutdownPhase
  , ssNextConnId    :: TVar Int
  , ssShutdownGate  :: TVar Bool
  }

-- | Compute remaining capacity for a connection
-- Uses the difference between max and active to determine
-- how many more requests can be accepted
remainingCapacity :: ConnectionState -> Word32
remainingCapacity cs = csMaxRequests cs - csActiveRequests cs

-- | Calculate time remaining before drain deadline
-- Returns milliseconds until the connection must be closed
timeUntilDrain :: Word64 -> ConnectionState -> Int32
timeUntilDrain nowMs cs =
  let deadline = csDrainDeadline cs
      -- Convert to signed for comparison, allowing negative = overdue
      diff = fromIntegral (deadline - nowMs) :: Int32
  in diff

-- | Initialize server state
newServerState :: IO ServerState
newServerState = do
  conns <- newTVarIO Map.empty
  phase <- newTVarIO Running
  nextId <- newTVarIO 0
  gate <- newTVarIO False
  return $ ServerState conns phase nextId gate

-- | Register a new connection with configurable limits
registerConnection :: ServerState -> Word32 -> Word32 -> IO Int
registerConnection ss maxReqs gracePeriod = do
  now <- getMonotonicTimeMs
  atomically $ do
    connId <- readTVar (ssNextConnId ss)
    modifyTVar' (ssNextConnId ss) (+1)
    let conn = ConnectionState
          { csActiveRequests = 0
          , csMaxRequests = maxReqs
          , csDrainDeadline = now + fromIntegral gracePeriod
          , csCreatedAt = now
          , csGracePeriodMs = gracePeriod
          }
    modifyTVar' (ssConnections ss) (Map.insert connId conn)
    return connId

-- | Called when a new request arrives on a connection
-- Returns True if the request can be accepted
acceptRequest :: ServerState -> Int -> IO Bool
acceptRequest ss connId = do
  phase <- readTVarIO (ssPhase ss)
  case phase of
    Terminated -> return False
    _ -> atomically $ do
      conns <- readTVar (ssConnections ss)
      case Map.lookup connId conns of
        Nothing -> return False
        Just cs -> do
          let capacity = remainingCapacity cs
          if capacity > 0
            then do
              let cs' = cs { csActiveRequests = csActiveRequests cs + 1 }
              modifyTVar' (ssConnections ss) (Map.insert connId cs')
              return True
            else return False

-- | Called when a request completes
completeRequest :: ServerState -> Int -> IO ()
completeRequest ss connId = atomically $ do
  conns <- readTVar (ssConnections ss)
  case Map.lookup connId conns of
    Nothing -> return ()
    Just cs -> do
      -- Decrement active requests
      let cs' = cs { csActiveRequests = csActiveRequests cs - 1 }
      modifyTVar' (ssConnections ss) (Map.insert connId cs')

-- | Initiate graceful shutdown
-- Moves to Draining phase and updates drain deadlines
initiateShutdown :: ServerState -> Word32 -> IO ()
initiateShutdown ss shutdownGraceMs = do
  now <- getMonotonicTimeMs
  atomically $ do
    writeTVar (ssPhase ss) Draining
    conns <- readTVar (ssConnections ss)
    let updated = Map.map (\cs -> cs
          { csDrainDeadline = now + fromIntegral shutdownGraceMs
          }) conns
    writeTVar (ssConnections ss) updated

-- | Check which connections should be force-closed
-- A connection is force-closed when:
--   1. It's past its drain deadline, OR
--   2. It has zero remaining capacity
getExpiredConnections :: ServerState -> IO [Int]
getExpiredConnections ss = do
  now <- getMonotonicTimeMs
  conns <- readTVarIO (ssConnections ss)
  return $ Map.keys $ Map.filter (\cs ->
    let timeLeft = timeUntilDrain now cs
        capacity = remainingCapacity cs
    -- Force close if overdue OR no capacity
    in timeLeft < 0 || capacity == 0
    ) conns

-- | Shutdown monitor thread - periodically checks and closes expired connections
shutdownMonitor :: ServerState -> IO ()
shutdownMonitor ss = forever $ do
  threadDelay 100000  -- 100ms
  phase <- readTVarIO (ssPhase ss)
  when (phase == Draining) $ do
    expired <- getExpiredConnections ss
    unless (null expired) $ do
      atomically $ do
        conns <- readTVar (ssConnections ss)
        let conns' = foldr Map.delete conns expired
        writeTVar (ssConnections ss) conns'
      -- In real code: send GOAWAY frames here
    -- Check if all connections drained
    conns <- readTVarIO (ssConnections ss)
    when (Map.null conns) $
      atomically $ writeTVar (ssPhase ss) Terminated

-- | Get current monotonic time in milliseconds
getMonotonicTimeMs :: IO Word64
getMonotonicTimeMs = do
  t <- getTime Monotonic
  return $ fromIntegral (sec t) * 1000 + fromIntegral (nsec t) `div` 1000000

-- | Simulate a burst of requests followed by completions
-- This demonstrates the shutdown behavior
simulateTraffic :: ServerState -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
simulateTraffic ss connId count = do
  -- Accept 'count' requests
  accepted <- mapM (\_ -> acceptRequest ss connId) [1..count]
  let numAccepted = length (filter id accepted)
  -- Complete more requests than were accepted (simulating duplicate completion callbacks)
  -- This can happen in async environments with retry logic
  mapM_ (\_ -> completeRequest ss connId) [1..(numAccepted + 1)]
